description:
Found by the reviewing session (s542) while probing s540d`s const-fold; PRE-EXISTING (main 24988e35 = the s540d tree; the fold does not reach it).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
  use constant ON => 1; use constant U => undef; sub g () { 6 }
  print "1 defined\n" if defined ON;        # perl prints; PCL prints NOTHING
  print "2 defined\n" if defined(ON);       # perl prints; PCL prints NOTHING
  print "3 defined\n" if defined ON();      # perl prints; PCL prints NOTHING
  my $x = defined ON; print "7 [$x]\n";     # perl [1]; PCL []
  print defined(g) ? "g" : "nog";           # both g  (a lower-case `()` sub is a call)

EMISSION: `(p-if (p-defined-fh (quote ON)) ...)`; for the lower-case sub `(p-defined (p-scalar-ctx (pl-g)))`.  So the bareword after `defined` is read as a FILEHANDLE by its spelling (upper case) before the callable question is asked.  Rule: a bare NAME is a call where it is CALLABLE (#266) -- a declared `()` constant in force at that point wins over the filehandle reading, as it does in the `print FOO, ...` slot (constants-01.t "Constant after print").

FIX DIRECTION (not built): the `defined BAREWORD` arm asks the prototype record in force (the parse clock, #2871) first; only an unknown bareword is a handle.  With s540d merged the same record carries the fold, so `defined ON` becomes `(p-defined 1)`.  Guard: a row in Pl/t/constants-01.t, perl-probed, incl. the `undef` constant (must stay false) and a real handle `defined STDIN` / `defined FH` (must stay a handle test).

SIBLINGS TO PROBE in the same batch (the same spelling test may sit in other handle-or-term slots): `eof NAME`, `fileno NAME`, `-t NAME`, `close NAME`, `tell NAME` with a declared constant NAME.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `defined NAME` / `defined(NAME)` / `defined NAME()` where NAME is an ALL-CAPS `use constant` is lowered `(p-defined-fh (quote NAME))` -- a filehandle test -- and answers FALSE; perl calls the constant and answers true
